alignments.note: The singular demonstrative is rendered by plural “these” with the dual noun.

The dual noun is rendered “two years.” Head moved to “years,” the token realizing the lemma שָׁנָה; “two” realizes the dual’s grammatical number, and the plural שָׁנִים in this same verse heads on “years” on the same ground (rule 24).
The noun takes its own English word.

The prepositional expression is the predicate and carries the supplied perfect copula under rule 49. Source head is the construct noun קֶרֶב, which rule 23 makes the head of a preposition fused with its construct, as לִפְנֵי does at GEN.45.5 and GEN.45.7 and עַל פִּי at GEN.45.21; the earlier reading headed it on the preposition.
The rectum’s article takes the written “the.”

The adverbial predicate of this verbless clause carries the construction-supplied frame “there are” together with its own “yet.” Rule 20 puts the presentative dummy in the unit that bears the copula and says it is never `added`; the earlier reading split “there” off as an `added` unit. The competing reading would give the copula instead to the numeral phrase, but nothing in it predicates and עוֹד is what the clause asserts.
The relative is rendered “in which,” headed on the relative word.
Existential carries the dummy, copula, and correlative negation, headed on the negation word under rule 50.
ASV renders the waw as the correlative “nor”; the present negative אֵין has already taken the opening “neither” under rule 14.

review_notes: Presentative “there” folded into the עוֹד unit under rule 20; the cleft and impersonal “It” elsewhere in the chapter remain `added`.
בְּ + קֶרֶב source head moved from the preposition to the construct noun (rule 23).
שְׁנָתַיִם target head moved from “two” to “years” (rule 24).
